svg.title: Stable workstation and child identities with revocable backend bindings
svg.desc: A protected native container verifies local direct children; its root is never a workspace registration. A purpose-authorized backend transaction validates epochs and request fingerprints, enforces unique installation, IP, child-name and Connect ID claims, and creates or reuses actual workstation, workspace and registration records. Workstation and child IDs are stable while IP and active binding revisions can change through an explicit confirmed rebind. Rebind revokes former sessions and preserves historical job origin. Non-default retirement fences admission and waits for genuinely drained associated work; incomplete or uncertain work keeps retirement pending. Tombstones remain, and recreating a deleted child name requires a new identity rather than reviving a retired record. The registry never creates or adopts a remote filesystem folder.
svg.text: Stable identities, unique claims, explicit binding changes
LOCAL OWNERSHIP PROOF AND BACKEND AUTHORITY ARE DISTINCT

g.text: Verified native container and child
Protected home root contains default + children
Local object / parent / marker checks precede use
Folder references use a contained child basename
Root is not registrable; no arbitrary path adoption
Purpose-authorized registry transaction
POST /api/v1/connect/registrations/ensure
Native registration permission + server-derived scope / access epoch
Shared transaction guard, unique claims and exact idempotent request fingerprint
A local marker describes identity; it does not authenticate a person or grant backend rights

svg.text: DURABLE BACKEND RECORDS · THE DEPLOYMENT OWNS THE REGISTRY

g.text: Workstation: stable ID
Scope + installation-marker hash identify it
Current canonical IP has one backend claim
IP is mutable through confirmed rebind
Observed peer address is diagnostic, not authority
Child workspace: stable ID
Belongs to one registered workstation
Unique child marker and canonical name claim
Default child may register; stays protected
Registry identity never means remote folder creation
Active backend binding
Registration ID + current independent revisions
IP:basename · [IPv6]:basename
Connect ID has one active registration claim
Collision fails; ensure never revives revocation
Rebind preserves identity and history
Require explicit rebind permission + confirmation
Retain workstation / child IDs; issue new bindings
Revoke former registrations and web sessions
Do not rewrite immutable accepted-job origins
Refresh locally stale child receipts before reuse
At most 256 active children; fail rather than truncate
Retire, drain and retain tombstones
Root / default cannot be retired or renamed
Fence admission; revoke sessions; await drain
Active causal work or uncertain effect: pending
No shared-work cancellation or history deletion
Recreated deleted name needs a new identity
Authoritative deletion-ready receipts permit cleanup
Web session / context lookup
Separately authorized server-only WebRelay
Unknown / revoked IDs never auto-register
Opaque token; authoritative 30-minute lifetime
Recheck binding, epochs and context revision
20 create attempts / minute / relay credential
Context selection is not a user credential

svg.text: The native filesystem manager owns folder containment and protected roots; the backend owns registry, sessions and admission.
Source contract only. No diagram node creates infrastructure, adopts a legacy root or proves a real Mac filesystem journey.
